events.title: Squarespace launched
events.summary: Anthony Casalena launched Squarespace in January 2004 from his University of Maryland dorm room — an all-in-one website builder and hosting platform.
events.about: Squarespace combined blogging, galleries, and styled templates without requiring HTML knowledge — a design-first alternative to WordPress and Blogger. Casalena was the sole developer until revenue hit $1 million in 2006; Squarespace later IPO'd on the NYSE in 2021.

narrative.whyChosen: Squarespace pioneered polished, template-driven site building for non-developers.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved design quality could be a product differentiator in website builders.
narrative.problemSolved: Creators wanted beautiful sites without learning code or patching together separate tools.

events.title: Scala first public release
events.summary: Martin Odersky released Scala publicly on January 20, 2004 — a language combining object-oriented and functional programming on the JVM.
events.about: Scala brought pattern matching, implicits, and actor-friendly concurrency to the Java ecosystem — later powering Twitter, Spark, and Akka. Scala 2.0 in 2006 stabilized the language for production use.

narrative.whyChosen: Scala introduced functional programming to mainstream JVM development.
narrative.whyImportant: It influenced Kotlin, Swift, and modern language design on managed runtimes.
narrative.problemSolved: JVM developers wanted expressive functional abstractions without abandoning Java interop.
